event: The Cloudflare tunnel program on the Mac grows old or its login breaks, and the tunnel stops carrying traffic.
trigger: Cloudflare supports only tunnel program versions within one year of the latest release. The version on the Mac, its update routine and the Cloudflare account owner are not recorded.
cost: Same as the server being down: all users lose scans until someone fixes it. Detection exists, repair is by hand on the Mac.
detect: GitHub alarm probes every 30 minutes and emails Jamin after two failures in a row.
response: 1. Check the tunnel job on the Mac. 2. Update the tunnel program and restart the job. 3. If the login is gone, sign in to Cloudflare and re-issue the credential.
smallest_fix: Write the three-step tunnel repair next to the backup restore notes and record the installed tunnel version once.
sources: .github/workflows/server-alarm.yml (probe schedule); https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/connections/connect-networks/downloads/ (one-year support window); mac/launchd/ (tunnel job)

event: A viral spike or a heavy user hits Cloudflare free-plan limits (request size, timeouts, rate rules) or the tunnel, and some requests fail.
trigger: Free plan limits are reported as 100 MB request body and a 100 to 120 second origin timeout (third-party sources disagree); the tunnel page itself states no limits.
cost: Failed scans during the spike, which is the moment of the most new users. Photo uploads are small, so the body limit is unlikely to bite; the cost is mainly from the Mac itself saturating.
detect: The 30-minute alarm would catch a full outage only; partial errors would show in the Mac's own error log, which nobody reads daily.
response: 1. Look at the Cloudflare analytics for the hour. 2. Check the Mac load. 3. Turn on stricter per-address limits already in the server.
smallest_fix: Read Cloudflare's official free-plan limits once and write the three that matter into the launch notes.
sources: https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/connections/connect-networks/ (no limits stated); web search 2026-11-18 (third-party figures, unconfirmed); settings/src/index.ts:75-104 (server-side rate defaults)

trigger: Backups rotate nightly at 04:00 and keep 14, so the oldest copy is about 15 days old. A silent corruption found on day 16 or later has no good copy to go back to; all copies are on the same disk.
cost: Loss of price history or device data with no way back; a PIPEDA breach record would also be needed if personal data were involved.
detect: A failed backup is not alerted anywhere (the job's script that actually runs lives outside the repo and was not read).
response: 1. Stop the server. 2. Restore the newest good backup. 3. Record what was lost.
response_exists: yes: docs/privacy/breach-plan.md (restore context); no restore guide for corruption
smallest_fix: Do one restore test from a backup now, and keep one monthly copy off the Mac.
sources: mac/launchd/com.shin.backup.plist (04:00 schedule); docs/privacy/data-requests.md (14 nights, about 15 days); docs/launch-gaps-2026-11-06.md

event: After a server restart, a deploy or a RevenueCat outage, paying users are treated as free users until their Plus status is looked up again.
trigger: Plus status is cached in memory for 10 minutes (60 seconds after an error) with a 120 a minute lookup limit. Every deploy restarts the server and empties the cache, so a wave of paying users looks up at once.
cost: Paying users briefly see the 10-a-week free limit, which risks refunds and bad reviews. Larger as subscribers grow, and each deploy repeats it.
detect: No test of this exists; nobody would know until a user complains.
response: 1. Raise the lookup limit. 2. Treat a lookup error as paid for a grace period. 3. Check the logs after each deploy.
smallest_fix: On a lookup failure or an over-limit lookup, keep the last known paid status for 24 hours; deploy in the middle of the night only.
sources: app/src/scan-quota.ts:49-54 (cache and limiter); https://api.revenuecat.com/v1/subscribers lookup in the same file

detect: The server logs source failures, but no alarm watches the rate of errors from Open Food Facts.
response: 1. Add a User-Agent with a contact address. 2. Raise the cache and keep results on disk. 3. If blocked, switch the source off and contact the project.
